newsitem.title: UK: Baby skeletons came from brothel - archaeologists.
newsitem.headline: Baby skeletons came from brothel - archaeologists.

text.p: A sad cache of baby skeletons beneath a bathhouse probably points to a Roman brothel in the biblical city of Ashkelon nearly 2,000 years ago, Israeli archaeologists reported on Wednesday.
Ariella Oppenheim of Hebrew University and colleagues said they had analysed about 100 skeletons found in a sewer beneath the ancient bathhouse in Ashkelon on Israel's southern coast.
The babies were both boys and girls, which meant they were not victims of the common Roman practice of female infanticide, they wrote in a letter to the science journal Nature.
Instead, they were probably dumped soon after birth by prostitutes, Oppenheim said.
"The infants' bones were mixed with animal bones, potsherds and coins in the gutter," they wrote.
They at first thought the babies must be girls abandoned by mothers wanting sons. But DNA analysis showed otherwise.

"The significant number of male victims was unexpected and raised the intriguing possibility that these infants may have been the unwanted offspring of courtesans working in the bathhouse," they concluded.
The fourth-century bathhouse bore a partial Greek inscription enjoining customers to "Enter, enjoy and...", indicating it might have been one of the brothels that were common in the Roman era.
